sources.name: Ant Design
sources.summary: An enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map covering components, the design language, and the token system. It links a full dump (llms-full.txt) that is ~2MB - reach for the semantic docs below instead of pulling it whole.

Ant Design's own design-language document: palette, tokens and values in the same shape as a DESIGN.md, written by the maintainers. Use it to theme an app to Ant Design rather than reverse-engineering the look.
Semantic component documentation (~750KB) covering component APIs precisely. Fetch it for API questions; too large to read whole.
Per-component docs and API, e.g. /components/table, /components/form.
Design-token based theming. Ant Design's tokens are the supported way to restyle it.

use_when: You are building an admin panel, console, or data-heavy internal tool.
You need forms and tables with serious built-in behaviour rather than primitives to assemble.
The product has a Chinese-market or enterprise audience where Ant Design is the familiar idiom.
You want Ant Design's own tokens and palette as a starting point - ant.design/design.md is a ready-made design-language document.
avoid_when: The surface is a marketing or consumer page - Ant Design is tuned for application chrome, not expressive layouts.
Bundle size on a small public site is a hard constraint.

baseline.description: An enterprise-class UI design language and React UI library

sources.name: Awesome DESIGN.md
sources.summary: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysing popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full design-language document for one brand: palette, type scale, spacing, component rules. This is the payload - read it before writing any UI.
Short human summary of that brand's design language.
The categorised index of every available brand. Read it to resolve a vague style request to a concrete brand slug.
Authoritative list of brand slugs currently in the repo - more reliable than the README when it lags.

use_when: Someone describes the look they want by naming a company ('make it feel like Linear').
You need a written design language before generating screens, so output stays consistent across a session.
You are seeding a new project and want a defensible starting palette and type scale.
avoid_when: You need runnable components - these are documents, not code.
The work is a public-facing product that would be mistaken for the analysed brand. Borrow the system, not the identity.

provides.name: 74 brand DESIGN.md profiles
provides.note: Slugs observed 2026-09-16: airbnb, airtable, apple, binance, bmw, bmw-m, bugatti, cal, claude, clay, clickhouse, cohere, coinbase, composio, cursor, dell-1996, elevenlabs, expo, ferrari, figma, framer, hashicorp, hp, ibm, intercom, kraken, lamborghini, linear.app, lovable, mastercard, meta, minimax, mintlify, miro, mistral.ai, mongodb, nike, nintendo-2001, notion, nvidia, ollama, opencode.ai, pinterest, playstation, posthog, raycast, renault, replicate, resend, revolut, runwayml, sanity, sentry, shopify, slack, spacex, spotify, starbucks, stripe, supabase, superhuman, tesla, theverge, together.ai, uber, vercel, vodafone, voltagent, warp, webflow, wired, wise, x.ai, zapier. Re-read the tree rather than trusting this list.

baseline.description: A collection of DESIGN.md files analysis by popular brand design systems. Drop one into your project and let coding agents generate a matching UI.

sources.notes: The DESIGN.md files describe real companies' visual systems. Use them as craft references and starting points. Do not reproduce another company's logo, wordmark, or trade dress in shipped work.

sources.name: ComfyUI
sources.summary: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

agent_entrypoints.what: Installation, node reference, and the workflow model.
The local server's HTTP and WebSocket routes - what to POST to /prompt, and how to follow progress. Read before driving an instance programmatically.
Local HTTP API of a running ComfyUI instance. POST a workflow graph as JSON to generate images programmatically; poll /history/{prompt_id} for results.
Install matrix, hardware requirements, supported model families.

use_when: A layout needs real imagery - hero art, textures, avatars, empty-state illustrations - and stock photos will not fit.
You want image generation running locally with reproducible, versionable workflow graphs.
You are producing many variants of the same asset and need a pipeline rather than one-off prompting.
avoid_when: You need UI components or design guidance. This is an image-generation backend, not a UI toolkit - it is indexed for the asset half of building an interface.
You want a zero-setup image API. Running it locally needs a GPU; the official desktop app and hosted cloud remove that, but both are their own setup and, for the cloud, their own cost.
The output would ship where the GPL-3.0 license or an individual model’s terms are a problem. Model weights carry their own licenses, separate from ComfyUI’s.

baseline.description: The most powerful and modular diffusion model GUI, api and backend with a graph/nodes interface.

sources.notes: Category outlier. ComfyUI is indexed as a visual-asset generator that feeds interface work, not as a UI library. It is also the only GPL-3.0 source in the catalog - relevant if anyone considers embedding rather than calling it. Its partner nodes call closed-source models (Nano Banana, Seedance and others) that carry their own terms and per-use cost, unlike the open weights it runs locally.

sources.name: Design Resources For Developers
sources.summary: Curated list of design and UI resources from stock photos, web templates, CSS frameworks, UI libraries, tools and much more.

agent_entrypoints.what: The entire list in one markdown file (~150KB). Fetch it and grep the section you need rather than reading it all. Note the lowercase filename.

use_when: You need raw material - a typeface, a photo source, an icon set, a mockup template - not code.
You want inspiration sources to look at before committing to a direction.
You need a chart or animation library and want a shortlist rather than a search engine.
avoid_when: You need opinionated guidance - this is breadth, deliberately unranked.
You need licensing certainty for a linked asset. Always check the destination's own terms before shipping anything from it.

provides.name: Sections
provides.note: 34 sections and roughly 1,100 links as of 2026-09-16. UI Graphics, Fonts, Colors, Icons, Logos, Favicons, Icon Fonts, Stock Photos, Stock Videos, Stock Music & Sound Effects, Vectors & Clip Art, Product & Image Mockups, HTML & CSS Templates, CSS Frameworks, CSS Methodologies, CSS Animations, Javascript Animation Libraries, Javascript Chart Libraries, UI Components & Kits, React/Vue/Angular/Svelte/React Native UI Libraries, Design Systems & Style Guides, Online Design Tools, Downloadable Design Software, Design Inspiration, Image Compression, Chrome Extensions, Firefox Extensions, AI Graphic Design Tools, Others.

baseline.description: Curated list of design and UI resources from stock photos, web templates, CSS frameworks, UI libraries, tools and much more

sources.notes: Links point to third-party sites with their own licenses and terms. The MIT license covers this list, not the resources it links to.

sources.name: Skills For Designers and Engineers
sources.summary: Skills for designers and engineers to help them build better user interfaces, focused on animation and interface craft, drawn from the author's experience at companies like Vercel and Linear.

agent_entrypoints.what: The full text of one skill, e.g. .../skills/review-animations/SKILL.md. Read the whole thing before applying it - the value is in the specific rules, not the summary. Not sure which? Read ask-emil, the router.
One page per skill with when to use it, an example result and prompts to try.

Installs the skill set into the user's own agent setup. Offer this when the user wants them permanently, rather than reading them ad hoc. The skills CLI sends anonymous usage data unless DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1 is set.

use_when: Anything is going to move. Read the animation skills before writing a transition, not after.
You need to choose between UI libraries and want a taste-informed answer instead of a download count.
You are reviewing UI that technically works but feels wrong.
A web app is being built or reviewed on a phone and feels like a website rather than something installed.
Fake data hides layout bugs: break-ui feeds a component long names, huge counts and empty lists before users do.
A session has had many design corrections and the next agent should not repeat them: learn-taste turns them into rules in DESIGN.md.
avoid_when: You need broad component coverage - this is craft guidance, not a component library.
You want a fixed set of checks run in CI. These are judgement skills for an agent to read; nothing here runs as a linter.

provides.name: emil-design-eng
provides.note: The main skill: mostly animation, plus general design advice.

provides.name: animate
provides.note: Builds an animation from scratch, choosing curve, duration and properties deliberately.

provides.name: animate-expo
provides.note: The same bar for React Native and Expo: gestures, sheets, haptics, motion off the JS thread.

provides.name: review-animations
provides.note: Strict review of existing animations.

provides.name: improve-animations
provides.note: Codebase-wide animation audit producing prioritized, self-contained plans.

provides.name: find-animation-opportunities
provides.note: Finds places motion would genuinely help - and says what not to animate.

provides.name: animation-vocabulary
provides.note: The right words to describe motion so an agent produces what you meant.

provides.name: apple-design
provides.note: Apple's interface and motion principles distilled from WWDC design talks, translated for the web.

provides.name: write-swift
provides.note: Modern Swift: value types, Swift 6 concurrency, generics, performance, Swift Testing.

provides.name: pick-ui-library
provides.note: Picks a trusted library instead of hand-rolling a toast or installing an abandoned package.

provides.name: prototype
provides.note: Builds several versions of a UI piece and gives you a switcher to compare them.

provides.name: mobile-native
provides.note: Makes a web app feel native on a phone: sticky hover, tap-highlight flashes, the 100vh bug, inputs that zoom, tap delay, safe areas and pull-to-refresh. Platform-layer CSS and meta tags, not motion - and not React Native, which is animate-expo.

provides.name: ask-sonner
provides.note: Working with Sonner, the author's toast library: setup, styling, recipes, fixes.

provides.name: remove-animations
provides.note: The opposite of finding opportunities: removes motion on keyboard actions, high-frequency surfaces and pure decoration.

provides.name: choreograph
provides.note: Coordinates several elements that animate together: what leads, what follows, what stays still.

provides.name: animation-performance
provides.note: Keeps animations inside the frame budget and finds the cause when one drops frames.

provides.name: gestures
provides.note: Drag, swipe and sheet interactions that track the finger 1:1 and stay interruptible.

provides.name: break-ui
provides.note: Feeds UI worst-case data - long names, missing fields, huge counts, zero items, non-Latin text - to find what breaks.

provides.name: learn-taste
provides.note: Turns a session's design corrections into rules, with their reasons, in DESIGN.md, a project skill or a lint check.

provides.name: ask-emil
provides.note: A router over the other skills: describe the situation and it names the skill or sequence to use.

sources.name: HyperFrames
sources.summary: A framework for turning HTML, CSS, media and seekable animations into deterministic MP4 videos, built for agents: a CLI to preview and render, skills that teach an agent to compose videos, and a catalog of blocks such as transitions, overlays and animated charts.

agent_entrypoints.what: Index of the docs (https://hyperframes.heygen.com/_llms/docs.txt) and of the block catalog (https://hyperframes.heygen.com/_llms/catalog.txt). Follow each index to the page you need.
One skill, e.g. .../skills/hyperframes/SKILL.md (composing a video) or .../skills/hyperframes-cli/SKILL.md (the CLI). Read the core one before writing a composition.
Scaffolds a video project; `npx hyperframes preview` opens a live preview and `npx hyperframes render` writes the MP4. Run with HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 (see notes).

use_when: A product needs a demo video, launch clip or social video and the team would rather write HTML and CSS than learn a video editor.
Interface motion or a UI walkthrough should become a video that renders the same every time.
An animated chart or data story is needed as a video file rather than a live page.
avoid_when: You are building the interface itself. This renders video; it is indexed for the marketing and demo half of shipping UI.
You need AI-generated footage, voice or music without paying - those come from HeyGen's models (the Studio app's Pro plan, or a HeyGen account for media-use), not from the open-source framework.
The environment has no Node 22 or cannot run a headless browser to render frames.

provides.name: hyperframes
provides.note: Read first: the render contract, the work loop and what each kind of video needs.

provides.name: hyperframes-cli
provides.note: Scaffold, check frames, edit timelines, preview, render and share.

provides.name: hyperframes-registry
provides.note: About 450 ready-made blocks installed as editable source: transitions, titles, captions, charts.

provides.name: media-use
provides.note: Getting or making music, images, voiceover and footage for a video, with HeyGen or free local tools.

provides.name: reverse-any-video
provides.note: Rebuilds an existing video as an editable project, checked frame by frame.

provides.name: style-sampling
provides.note: A new episode in one of a few proven explainer styles.

provides.name: slideshow
provides.note: A deck to present live, served by `hyperframes present`. Installed on demand.

provides.name: figma
provides.note: Brings Figma assets, tokens and frames into a video. Installed on demand.

provides.name: remotion-to-hyperframes
provides.note: Ports Remotion, Lottie, Motion Canvas or plain CSS animation. Installed on demand.

baseline.description: AI video you can actually edit. HyperFrames is a free, open-source AI video editor. Describe any video and get a real project you can change down to the frame.

sources.notes: Category outlier, like ComfyUI: indexed for the media that ships alongside an interface. The CLI sends anonymous usage data to PostHog by default; set HYPERFRAMES_NO_TELEMETRY=1 or DO_NOT_TRACK=1. The framework is Apache-2.0 with no per-render fees; the separate Studio app has a paid Pro plan.

sources.name: Impeccable
sources.summary: The design vocabulary for a coding agent: commands to steer a design (bolder, quieter, distill, typeset), review it (critique, audit) and finish it (polish, harden), plus a deterministic detector of 62 rules that flags the tells of AI-made UI. Started from Anthropic's frontend-design skill.

agent_entrypoints.what: Index of the current docs: workflows, every command's page, the detector and configuration. Start here to find the page for one command before running it.
The skill itself as built for Claude Code. Read it to see how a command is routed before installing anything.
The catalog of AI-made UI anti-patterns the detector looks for, with examples. Reach for it when writing or justifying a "this looks AI-made" finding.

Runs the detector with no agent and no API key and prints findings as JSON. Point it at a dev-server URL instead of a folder to get the rules that need a rendered page, such as contrast and tiny text. `--list-rules` prints every rule.
Installs the skill into the user's agent setup and offers the edit hook. Offer it only when the user wants it permanently, and say what the hook and telemetry do first (see notes).

use_when: A screen works but looks generic or AI-made and you need named, rule-based findings rather than taste.
You want a deterministic slop check in CI: the detector emits JSON, GitHub annotations or SARIF and needs no model.
You need a word for the change you want ("quieter", "distill", "typeset") so the agent makes one targeted move instead of a redesign.
A UX critique or accessibility/performance audit is wanted with findings ranked by severity.
avoid_when: You cannot accept install-time side effects: the optional edit hook runs on every UI file the agent edits, runs even when the model's own commands are denied, and downloads an engine binary into ~/.impeccable/bin/ on first use.

The run is unattended and live mode is on: when no chat session is polling, Apply launches the codex or claude CLI with approvals and sandboxing bypassed. Set IMPECCABLE_LIVE_COPY_AGENT=chat (or off) before starting live mode.
You only need one or two checks on a native app - the detector, live mode and the hook are web-only.
The project has a signed design direction the commands would argue with; it brings its own opinions about what good looks like.

provides.name: critique
provides.note: Scored UX review against usability heuristics, ranked by what to fix first.

provides.name: audit
provides.note: Technical report on accessibility, performance, theming and responsive behaviour, ranked P0 to P3.

provides.name: polish
provides.note: Final pass before shipping.

provides.name: harden
provides.note: Errors, i18n, overflow and edge cases.

provides.name: distill
provides.note: Removes what the page does not need.

provides.name: onboard
provides.note: First-run flows and empty states.

provides.name: detect
provides.note: The 62-rule deterministic slop detector, as a CLI, an edit hook and a Chrome extension.

provides.name: live
provides.note: Pick an element in the running dev server and cycle through variants in place.

baseline.description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent. Steer with polish and bolder, review with critique and audit, catch AI slop before it ships.

sources.notes: Telemetry is on by default: it records which visual directions were shown and picked (not code or files). Turn it off with `npx impeccable telemetry off` or DO_NOT_TRACK=1; the request that fetches directions still happens. The skill, CLI, hook and detector are free; a paid Pro plan adds extra detector rules and pull-request reviews. Ships builds for many agents from one repository, so the repo root is mostly per-tool folders.

sources.name: Material UI
sources.summary: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design. Free forever.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map for Material UI, linking a .md version of every component page. Note the /material-ui/ path segment; the site root has no llms.txt.
Clean markdown for one component page, e.g. react-button.md, react-autocomplete.md. Prefer this over the HTML page - same content, far cheaper to read.
Per-component documentation, e.g. react-button, react-autocomplete, react-data-grid.
The theming system. Read before overriding styles ad hoc - MUI's theme is the intended customization surface.

use_when: The project already uses Material UI, or the team explicitly wants Material Design.
You need a large, genuinely complete component set under one MIT license - the core @mui/material package covers autocomplete, tables, dialogs, forms and the rest.
The audience is enterprise or internal-tools and density plus familiarity beat novelty.
You want theming through a real API rather than overrides - createTheme is the supported customization surface.
avoid_when: The brief calls for a distinctive look - Material UI reads as Material unless you invest real effort in the theme.
The project is already on Tailwind plus a copy-in component set; mixing the two styling models causes more pain than it solves.

You are counting on advanced data-grid or date-picker features being free. Those live in MUI X, a separate product: its MIT versions are free forever, but the advanced features need a Pro or Premium commercial license. Check the tier before promising a feature.

baseline.description: Material UI: Comprehensive React component library that implements Google's Material Design. Free forever.

sources.notes: The MIT license covers the core Material UI library. MUI X (Data Grid, Date and Time Pickers, Charts, Tree View) is a separate product with MIT, Pro and Premium tiers - the Pro and Premium features are commercially licensed. Verify which tier a feature needs before recommending it.

sources.name: Playwright CLI
sources.summary: A command-line interface into Playwright built for coding agents, with a skill: open a page, click, type, take screenshots and accessibility snapshots, emulate devices and inspect the network, without loading large tool schemas or page trees into the model's context.

agent_entrypoints.what: The skill an agent follows to drive the CLI. Read it before scripting a check of a running UI.

Every command, written so an agent can learn the tool from it with no skill installed. Install first with `npm install -g @playwright/cli@latest`; `playwright-cli install --skills` adds the skill locally.
The human-facing guide to the CLI on the Playwright site.

use_when: An agent has built or changed a screen and must see it: screenshots at phone and desktop sizes, the empty and error states, keyboard flow.
You need an accessibility snapshot of a page to check labels, roles and heading order.
Browser checks have to fit in a long agent session where an MCP server's schemas and page trees would eat the context.
avoid_when: You need a long-lived browser the agent reasons over step by step (exploratory or self-healing tests) - Playwright's own docs point to Playwright MCP for that.
The project already has a Playwright test suite or a browser tool wired into its agent; use what is there.
You need pixel-diff visual regression across commits. This takes screenshots; it does not compare them for you.

baseline.description: CLI for common Playwright actions. Record and generate Playwright code, inspect selectors and take screenshots.

sources.name: shadcn/ui
sources.summary: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented map of the docs. Start here to learn install flow, conventions, and what exists.
Machine-readable list of every registry item with per-item docs, API and example links. Use it to answer 'does a component for X exist' without guessing.
The actual source of one component for one style, e.g. .../new-york-v4/button.json. Returns the files you would copy in.
The full color scale set. Use for building a theme rather than inventing hex values.

shadcn/ui's own skill for AI assistants. It reads the project's components.json and supplies the framework, aliases, installed components, icon and base library, so generated code matches the project. Install it with the skills CLI when the user wants it permanently.
Community registries built into the CLI. Check here before concluding a component does not exist - the core registry is not the whole ecosystem.
Installs a component into the user's project. Prefer this over pasting code you generated.

use_when: The project is React-flavoured and uses Tailwind, and you need real components fast.
You want to own the component source rather than depend on a black-box package.
You need an accessible primitive (dialog, combobox, popover) and hand-rolling one would be a mistake.
You need a coherent theme and want token values that already work in light and dark.
You are building your own component library or internal registry, not just consuming components.
avoid_when: The project is not React-based - the registry assumes React component files.
The team wants a batteries-included library it never has to maintain; here the code becomes yours.

baseline.description: Composable, accessible components with thoughtful defaults. Build your own component library with code you can customize, extend, and make your own.

sources.name: Storybook
sources.summary: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation.

agent_entrypoints.what: Agent-oriented docs map: setup per framework, writing stories, testing, addons.
Storybook's own agent integration: skills, the MCP server, and agentic review. Read this before wiring an agent to a Storybook.
Storybook MCP server. Lets an agent list stories, read their args and run their tests, so it can see the components it built instead of guessing.
Append .md to any docs URL for clean markdown with code examples, e.g. /docs/writing-stories/decorators.md. Much cheaper than scraping the HTML page.
Adds Storybook to an existing project, detecting the framework.
Full documentation when llms.txt is not specific enough.

use_when: You generated several components and the user needs to actually see and compare them.
You want states (loading, empty, error, long text) to be reviewable without clicking through the whole app.
You need a durable home for a design system's documentation.
You want visual or accessibility regressions caught automatically.
An agent needs to see the components it built, rather than assert they work - the MCP server exposes stories and their tests.
avoid_when: It is a one-off prototype that will be deleted this week - the setup cost will not pay back.
The user asked for a static mockup with no build step.

provides.name: MCP server and agent skills
provides.note: Added in Storybook 10: CLI bindings for agent tools, an MCP server, and agentic review. React is stable; Angular-Vite and Vue support are experimental as of 10.6.

provides.name: Vitest addon
provides.note: Runs stories as component tests, so every state you documented is also a test.

provides.name: Accessibility addon
provides.note: Automated a11y checks per story - catches a real fraction of what a manual review would.

baseline.description: Storybook is the industry standard workshop for building, documenting, and testing UI components in isolation

sources.name: UI SDK

author.name: Vercel Labs
author.credit_note: Most of the work is by shadcn (https://github.com/shadcn), creator of shadcn/ui.

sources.summary: A library of behaviours for agents to build interfaces with: keyboard navigation, focus, selection, dismissal, popups, drag and drop and their ARIA, in a framework-free core with adapters for React, Vue, Svelte, Solid and Web Components, plus unstyled components and an agent skill for building missing ones from the same parts.

agent_entrypoints.what: Index of the docs. From here, read your framework's llms.txt (e.g. https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/llms.txt) for every component's parts and props, or Core to build a component it does not ship.
The agent skill: choosing and composing its components, building a missing one from core behaviours, making the page usable by agents, and testing keyboard, focus and ARIA.
The Web Components docs in one file, for a page with no build step that loads web.js and web.css from the site.
Installs the skill into the user's agent setup. Prefix with DISABLE_TELEMETRY=1 - the skills CLI sends anonymous usage data by default.

use_when: You need a component with real keyboard, focus and ARIA behaviour (select, combobox, menu, dialog) and want to bring your own styles.
The component you need does not exist in any library (a stepper, a splitter, a transfer list) and you want to build it from tested behaviours instead of by hand.
One behaviour layer has to serve several frameworks, or Web Components.
An in-app agent should operate the page: it exposes the page's controls to an agent without screenshots.
avoid_when: You need a stable API: it is in beta (0.1.0 pre-releases, first published October 2026) under Vercel's beta terms, and the API may change before general availability.
You want a finished look out of the box. Components render no styles of their own beyond an optional default stylesheet.
The project already uses a mature headless library well - switching costs more than it buys while this is in beta.

baseline.description: A library of behaviors for agents to build the next generation of user interfaces.

sources.notes: Beta. Repository created 2026-10-26; recheck the API and the beta label at each review. Docs ship inside each npm package (node_modules/@ui-sdk/<framework>/docs/llms.txt), which matches the installed version better than the website.

sources.name: UI UX Pro Max
sources.summary: An AI skill that provides design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms, including a design-system generator, a searchable style taxonomy, and per-stack component catalogs.

agent_entrypoints.what: One skill's instructions. Skills present at last index: banner-design, brand, design-system, design, slides, ui-styling, ui-ux-pro-max.
The searchable style taxonomy as CSV. Useful for mapping a loose aesthetic brief onto named styles.
Per-stack component and library catalog, e.g. stacks/nextjs.csv, stacks/shadcn.csv, stacks/flutter.csv, stacks/swiftui.csv.

Topic datasets: app-interface, charts, colors, google-fonts, icons, landing, motion, products, react-performance, styles, typography (74 font pairings), ui-reasoning (192 per-category UI profiles with anti-patterns), ux-guidelines (119 do/don’t rules with code examples).
The project's own installer and design-system commands.

use_when: You need a full design system proposed from a project brief rather than assembled by hand.
The target stack is outside the React/Tailwind mainstream and you need stack-appropriate component suggestions.
You want a named, searchable style rather than an improvised aesthetic.
You want a font pairing, a UX do/don’t checklist, or a per-category UI pattern rather than a whole design system.
avoid_when: You only need one component - reaching for a whole design-system generator is overkill.

provides.name: Agent skills
provides.note: banner-design, brand, design, design-system, slides, ui-styling, ui-ux-pro-max.

provides.name: Per-stack catalogs
provides.note: 22 CSVs under cli/assets/data/stacks/: angular, astro, avalonia, flutter, html-tailwind, javafx, jetpack-compose, laravel, nextjs, nuxt-ui, nuxtjs, react, react-native, shadcn, svelte, swiftui, threejs, uno, uwp, vue, winui, wpf.

provides.name: Topic datasets
provides.note: 13 CSVs under cli/assets/data/, including typography (font pairings with moods and Google Fonts imports), ui-reasoning (recommended pattern, palette and anti-patterns per UI category) and ux-guidelines (do/don’t rules with good and bad code, by severity).

baseline.description: An AI skill that provides design intelligence for building professional UI/UX across multiple platforms.

sources.notes: The repository is the free tier of a project that also sells a premium version. Everything indexed here is from the MIT-licensed open repository.
